Label: Lung Meridian
Synonym: Lung Meridian of Hand-Taiyin, meridian of the lung, LU
Description: The Lung meridian (LU) consists of 11 acupuncture points which begins at LU 1 (Zhongfu) on the upper anterior chest, lateral to the infraclavicular fossa, travels down the anterior-lateral aspect of the arm, and ends at LU 11 (Shaoshang) on the radial side of the thumb near the corner of the nail.
Reference: WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations in the Western Pacific Region. World Health Organization (WHO), WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific, 2008. https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/353407

Label: Large Intestine Meridian
Synonym: Large Intestine Meridian of Hand-Yangming, meridian of the large intestine, LI
Chinese Label: 手陽(阳)明大腸(肠)經(经,経)
Description: The Large Intestine meridian (LI) consists of 20 acupuncture points which begins at LI 1 (Shangyang) on the radial side of the index finger near the corner of the nail, travels up the dorsal-radial aspect of the arm, crosses over the shoulder and the side of the neck to the face, and ends at LI 20 (Yingxiang) in the nasolabial sulcus beside the ala of the nose.
Reference: WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations in the Western Pacific Region. World Health Organization (WHO), WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific, 2008. https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/353407

Label: Stomach Meridian
Synonym: Stomach Meridian of Foot-Yangming, meridan of the stomach, ST
Description: The Stomach meridian (ST) consists of 45 acupuncture points which begins at ST 1 (Chengqi) on the face, between the eyeball and the infraorbital margin directly below the pupil, travels down across the face, neck, chest, and abdomen, continues down the anterior-lateral aspect of the leg, and ends at ST 45 (Lidui) on the lateral side of the second toe near the corner of the nail.
Reference: WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations in the Western Pacific Region. World Health Organization (WHO), WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific, 2008. https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/353407

Label: Spleen Meridian
Synonym: Spleen Meridian of Foot-Taiyin, meridian of the spleen, SP
Description: The Spleen meridian (SP) consists of 21 acupuncture points which begins at SP 1 (Yinbai) on the medial side of the great toe near the corner of the nail, travels up along the medial aspect of the leg, continues up the abdomen and chest, and ends at SP 21 (Dabao) on the lateral thorax in the sixth intercostal space on the midaxillary line.
Reference: WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations in the Western Pacific Region. World Health Organization (WHO), WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific, 2008. https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/353407

Label: Heart Meridian
Synonym: Heart Meridian of Hand-Shaoyin, meridian of the heart, HT
Description: The Heart meridian (HT) consists of 9 acupuncture points which begins at HT 1 (Jiquan) in the center of the axillary fossa, travels down the medial aspect of the arm, and ends at HT 9 (Shaochong) on the radial side of the little finger near the corner of the nail.
Reference: WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations in the Western Pacific Region. World Health Organization (WHO), WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific, 2008. https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/353407

Label: Small Intestine Meridian
Synonym: Small Intestine Meridian of Hand-Taiyang, meridian of the small intenstine, SI
Chinese Label: 手太陽(阳)小腸(肠)經(经,経)
Description: The Small Intestine meridian (SI) consists of 19 acupuncture points which begins at SI 1 (Shaoze) on the ulnar side of the little finger near the corner of the nail, travels up the dorsal-ulnar aspect of the arm, crosses the scapular region, and ascends along the lateral neck and cheek, ending at SI 19 (Tinggong) in the depression between the tragus and the mandibular condyloid process.
Reference: WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations in the Western Pacific Region. World Health Organization (WHO), WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific, 2008. https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/353407

Label: Bladder Meridian
Synonym: Bladder Meridian of Foot-Taiyang, meridian of the bladder, meridan of the urinary bladder, urinary bladder meridian, BL, UB
Description: The Bladder meridian (BL) consists of 67 acupuncture points which begins at BL 1 (Jingming) on the face in the depression just superior to the inner canthus of the eye, travels up over the head, descends down the back in two parallel lines flanking the spine, continues along the posterior aspect of the leg, and ends at BL 67 (Zhiyin) on the lateral side of the little toe near the corner of the nail.
Reference: WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations in the Western Pacific Region. World Health Organization (WHO), WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific, 2008. https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/353407

Label: Kidney Meridian
Synonym: Kidney Meridian of Foot-Shaoyin, meridian of the kidney, KI
Description: The Kidney meridian (KI) consists of 27 acupuncture points which begins at KI 1 (Yongquan) on the sole of the foot in the depression formed when the toes are flexed, travels up along the medial aspect of the leg, continues up the abdomen and chest close to the midline, and ends at KI 27 (Shufu) on the anterior chest in the depression at the inferior border of the clavicle.
Reference: WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations in the Western Pacific Region. World Health Organization (WHO), WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific, 2008. https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/353407

Label: Pericardium Meridian
Synonym: Pericardium Meridian of Hand-Jueyin, meridian of the pericardiam, PC
Chinese Label: 手厥陰(阴)心包(包)經(经,経)
Description: The Pericardium meridian (PC) consists of 9 acupuncture points which begins at PC 1 (Tianchi) on the anterior chest in the fourth intercostal space, lateral to the nipple, travels down the middle of the anterior aspect of the arm, and ends at PC 9 (Zhongchong) at the center of the tip of the middle finger.
Reference: WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations in the Western Pacific Region. World Health Organization (WHO), WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific, 2008. https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/353407

Label: Triple Energizer Meridian
Synonym: Triple Energizer Meridian of Hand-Shaoyang, meridian of triple energizer, Triple Warmer Meridian, Triple Heater Meridian, Triple Burner Meridan, San Jiao, Sanjiao, TE, TW, SJ, TB
Description: The Triple Energizer meridian (TE) consists of 23 acupuncture points which begins at TE 1 (Guanchong) on the ulnar side of the ring finger near the corner of the nail, travels up the dorsal-middle aspect of the arm, ascends over the shoulder and the side of the neck, and circles around the ear, ending at TE 23 (Sizhukong) in the depression at the lateral end of the eyebrow.
Reference: WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations in the Western Pacific Region. World Health Organization (WHO), WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific, 2008. https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/353407

Label: Gallbladder Meridian
Synonym: Gallbladder Meridian of Foot-Shaoyang, meridian of the gallbladder, meridian of the gall bladder, gall bladder meridian, GB
Description: The Gallbladder meridian (GB) consists of 44 acupuncture points which begins at GB 1 (Tongziliao) on the head in the depression lateral to the outer canthus of the eye, zigzags across the temporal and occipital regions of the head, descends along the lateral side of the neck, trunk, and leg, and ends at GB 44 (Zuqiaoyin) on the lateral side of the fourth toe near the corner of the nail.
Reference: WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations in the Western Pacific Region. World Health Organization (WHO), WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific, 2008. https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/353407

Label: Liver Meridian
Synonym: Liver Meridian of Foot-Jueyin, meridian of the liver, LR
Description: The Liver meridian (LR) consists of 14 acupuncture points which begins at LR 1 (Dadun) on the lateral side of the great toe near the corner of the nail, travels up along the medial aspect of the leg, passes through the genital region and abdomen, and ends at LR 14 (Qimen) on the anterior chest in the sixth intercostal space.
Reference: WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations in the Western Pacific Region. World Health Organization (WHO), WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific, 2008. https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/353407

Label: Governor Vessel
Synonym: Du Channel, Du, GV, Du Mai
Description: The Governor Vessel (GV / Du Mai) consists of 28 acupuncture points which begins at GV 1 (Changqiang) in the perineal region midway between the tip of the coccyx and the anus, travels up along the posterior midline of the body over the spine and across the top of the head, and ends at GV 28 (Yinjiao) in the oral cavity at the frenulum of the upper lip.
Reference: WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations in the Western Pacific Region. World Health Organization (WHO), WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific, 2008. https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/353407

Label: Conception Vessel
Synonym: Ren Channel, RN, CV, Ren, Ren Mai
Description: The Conception Vessel (CV / Ren Mai) consists of 24 acupuncture points which begins at CV 1 (Huiyin) in the perineum at the midpoint of the perineal region, travels up along the anterior midline of the body through the abdomen, chest, and neck, and ends at CV 24 (Chengjiang) on the face in the depression at the center of the mentolabial sulcus.
Reference: WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations in the Western Pacific Region. World Health Organization (WHO), WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific, 2008. https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/353407
